sovereign_country.strategic_role: 拉美美元金融中枢、私人利益基金会（PIF）与运河船舶登记

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Intermodal ISO Shipping Container Fleet Asset Leasing

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid – Civil law foundation with strong Anglo-American corporation-law influence and commercial practice; unitary national legislation.
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Panama-United States Trade Promotion Agreement (TPA), in force since 31 October 2012, including its investment chapter.
Panama-Spain Agreement for the Promotion and Reciprocal Protection of Investments (APPRI), currently in force.
Panama-Netherlands Bilateral Investment Treaty, currently in force.
Panama-Singapore Double Taxation Avoidance Agreement (DTAA), currently in force.
Panama-Spain Double Taxation Avoidance Agreement (DTAA), currently in force.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Ley 23 de 2015, as amended, provides the national AML/CFT framework; Decreto Ejecutivo No. 406 de 2019, as amended, regulates customer due diligence, beneficial-owner identification and PEP/sanctions control; Ley 70 de 2019 establishes the final beneficial owner (Beneficiario Final) regime; Ley 129 de 2020 and its implementing regulations create the Final Beneficiary Registry administered by the Registro Público de Panamá; Decreto de Gabinete No. 3 de 1987, as amended, governs the creation and operation of Sociedades Anónimas.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access – UBO declarations are filed with the Registro Público de Panamá and are accessible only to competent national authorities and international partners pursuant to law; no public UBO search portal exists; nominee arrangements are permitted but mandatory disclosure of the natural-person final beneficiary remains absolute.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized certified copy of the beneficial owner's and director's passport identification pages
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille issued by the competent authority of the country of origin; if the origin state is not a Hague Convention member, consular legalization by a Panamanian consul

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Original notarial Power of Attorney (Poder General) appointing the Panamanian resident agent and incorporator
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the applicant's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or, for non-Hague states, Panamanian consular legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Final Beneficiary Declaration (Declaración Jurada de Beneficiario Final) completed by each ultimate beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Applicant/ultimate beneficial owner before a notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization, with sworn Spanish translation where the original is in another language

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Unavailability of Corporate Name (Certificado de Nombre No Registrado)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registro Público de Panamá, Sección de Personas Jurídicas
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized only; not subject to apostille because issued by the Panamanian registry itself

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-acceptance screening against: (i) Panama's integrated PEP database and UAF guidelines; (ii) OFAC SDN and consolidated sanctions lists; (iii) UN Security Council Consolidated List; (iv) EU consolidated financial sanctions list; and (v) any domestic Panamanian restrictive measures. Screening must be conducted at onboarding and at least annually thereafter; any positive match triggers enhanced due diligence, source-of-funds verification and, where appropriate, a suspicious transaction report to the Unidad de Análisis Financiero (UAF). Records must be maintained for a minimum of five years.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Público de Panamá – Sede Electrónica (Servicio de Certificado de Nombre de Personas Jurídicas)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names are filed in the Spanish-language registry system and must be expressed in Latin script. Diacritics may be normalized to the registry's character set. The distinguishing name must not be identical or deceptively similar to an existing registered name; names may be in a foreign language, but a Spanish transliteration is required for registry indexing and publication.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the Registro Público rejects or conditionally objects to the proposed name, the incorporator may file a written reconsideration (recurso de reconsideración) with the Director General of the Registro Público within five business days of the rejection notice, providing comparative citations of earlier registrations or evidence of government or industry consent where applicable. If the reconsideration is denied, an administrative appeal may be filed with the Registro's superior administrative body, and a contested-administrative-annulment action (demanda contencioso-administrativa) may be brought before the Sala Tercera of the Corte Suprema de Justicia within the statutory two-month period from final rejection. The 30-day name certificate cannot be broadly extended; after expiry, or after a final adverse decision, the applicant must submit a fresh name-clearance request accompanied by the applicable new tariff.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A pure virtual registered office is not permissible. The Sociedad Anónima must maintain a physical registered office in Panama at the address of its duly licensed resident agent. A virtual/administrative correspondence address may be used for non-statutory back-office purposes, but it cannot replace the statutory registered office required by Decreto de Gabinete No. 3 de 1987.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low (approximately 2% annual probability). The target activity—intermodal ISO shipping-container fleet leasing under ISIC 5229/NAICS 532411—is not a licensed financial, insurance or fiduciary operation. It does not create a high probability of unannounced premises inspection; nevertheless, the Registro Público, UAF, DGI and customs authorities retain the right to conduct random inspections where books, UBO records and registered-office existence are verified.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Pre-clearance corporate name search and certificate of name availability
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official statutory tariff for name certificates

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Drafting and notarization of the Articles of Incorporation (Pacto Social y Estatutos) and incorporation minutes
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Notary Public and Panamanian corporate attorney
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for a standard Sociedad Anónima with no licensed activity

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Public Registry inscription and certificate of incorporation issuance
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official registry tariff for inscription of personas jurídicas

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Initial Final Beneficiary Registry declaration filing
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Registro Público de Panamá / UBO Registry

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: First-year licensed resident agent and physical registered office service
Apostille or consular legalization of foreign-issued UBO, passport and power-of-attorney documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Competent apostille/consular authority plus Panamanian notary for translation

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: KYC/AML file setup, PEP and sanctions screening, UBO piercing and compliance onboarding
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Compliance service provider / corporate law firm

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Corporate seal, first statutory books and common-share certificate drafting

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Ley 32 de 1927 (Código de Comercio), Libro II, Título IV, Arts. 128-208, as amended by Ley 3 de 2016, Ley 44 de 2008, and implementing decrees on beneficial ownership and corporate records.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Público de Panamá, Departamento de Registro de Documentos Mercantiles, acting upon notarization by an authorized Panamanian Notario Público.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Public Deed of Incorporation and Articles of Association (Escritura Pública de Constitución y Estatutos).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital and no escrow account requirement. The charter ordinarily designates an authorised capital of 10,000 shares without par value; shares may be issued for such consideration as the board determines, and non-resident shareholders may hold 100% of the capital.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION: The undersigned directors, constituting the entire board, unanimously resolve: (1) approve the Public Deed of Incorporation and Articles of Association; (2) issue the full authorised capital of 10,000 shares without par value to the subscribers named in the deed, each subscriber paying the amount fixed by the directors; (3) adopt the registered office located in Panama City, Republic of Panama, care of the appointed resident agent; (4) appoint the officers listed in the first annual report, including President, Secretary and Treasurer; (5) authorise the officers to open bank accounts, execute lease agreements, and perform all acts necessary for the company’s operations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name search and reservation at the Public Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Dirección de Registro Electrónico (eRegistro) or the Mercantile Section at the main registry office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit three alternative corporate names in order of preference, together with the notarised power of attorney of the incorporators if acting through a local agent. The registry performs a phonetic and exact-match search against existing companies and, if clear, grants a name reservation for a non-extendable period.
required_dossiers: Notarised power of attorney (Poder Especial) in favour of the resident agent
Completed application form with three candidate names
Certified copy of passport or ID of each incorporator
Payment receipt for name search and reservation fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused or competing, the registry issues a written note; the applicant may submit a revised list of alternatives, and any administrative refusal may be appealed before the Senior Registrar within five business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting of the public deed and articles of association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notario Público with active license in Panama; the local attorney/firm coordinating the formation.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The attorney prepares the Escritura Pública containing the company name, registered agent, directors, officers, purpose, capital structure, and bylaw articles. The draft is circulated to the incorporators for final approval before execution.
required_dossiers: Approved draft of the Articles of Association
Full legal name, domicile, and passport copy of each shareholder and director
Registered office address and resident agent services agreement
Statement of intended purpose, including ISIC 5229 container fleet leasing
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary or counsel identifies inconsistencies in the corporate purpose or capital clauses, the draft is revised and re-circulated before notarization; no registry query applies at this stage.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution and notarization of the incorporation instrument
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The incorporators or their legal representatives appear before the notary to sign the public deed. The notary authenticates the signatures, verifies identity, and records any power of attorney used. The instrument receives a notarial protocol number and is ready for registry presentation.
required_dossiers: Original draft of the public deed
Passport or valid Panamanian ID of each signatory
Certified copies of powers of attorney, if applicable
Initial directors’ acceptance in written form
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If identity documents are expired or signatures are inconsistent, the notary refuses execution and the entity must correct documentation or grant a fresh power of attorney before rescheduling.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration with the Public Registry – Mercantile Section
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá, Departamento de Registro de Documentos Mercantiles
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the original public deed, together with a certified copy and the name reservation certificate (if used). The registry assigns a folio number, scrutinises compliance with the Commercial Code, and records the company in the mercantile register.
required_dossiers: Original Notarised Public Deed of Incorporation
Certified copy of the deed for the registry file
Name reservation certificate, if previously obtained
Official fee deposit slip for registry registration
Certified copy of the first board resolution appointing officers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues formal observations (observaciones), the company’s attorney must submit a correction deed or written clarification within the statutory window, after which the file is re-presented with the required fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the registry issues the certified company certificate, the company must obtain a tax identification number (RUC) through the DGI portal, update the registered address, and register as a territorial taxpayer. The DGI will issue the company’s cédula and tax declaration forms.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of the company registration certificate
Public deed of incorporation
Directors’ and resident agent’s identification documents
Sworn statement of the commencement of operations or intention to remain inactive
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the DGI requires further information on economic activity, the taxpayer submits supplementary declarations through the virtual office or attends a personal hearing; an appeal may be lodged with the Revenue Appeals Directorate if the registration is unreasonably withheld.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Business licence application or statutory exemption confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministerio de Comercio e Industrias (MICI), Ventanilla Única de Inversión / PanamaEmprende
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: For an ISIC 5229 container leasing activity conducted from Panama with no physical local establishment, the company files a sworn statement confirming the absence of a permanent facility and requests an exemption from the industrial licence obligation. If a local office is later opened, the company must obtain the standard Aviso de Operación.
required_dossiers: Company registration certificate
RUC certificate
Sworn declaration of non-establishment, if claiming exemption
Copy of the first board resolution identifying the commencement date
Proof of payment of the municipal notice fee, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If MICI determines that a local establishment exists or will exist, the applicant must obtain an Aviso de Operación within fifteen business days and may face inspection; remediation is completed by submitting the licence application and paying the corresponding fees.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministerio de Comercio e Industrias (MICI) – Dirección de Empresas, within the national business registry system (PanamaEmprende).
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Exempt – ISIC 5229 constitutes non-industrial equipment leasing. No manufacturing or plant operating permit is required; a municipal Aviso de Operación would be needed only if a physical local office is opened.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio de Ambiente (MiAMBIENTE), Dirección de Evaluación de Impacto Ambiental
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Categoría III – Exempt for pure container fleet leasing without stationary physical facilities; a full or partial Environmental Impact Study will be triggered only if warehousing, container repair, or fuel storage operations are established.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable in the exempt state. In the event of future activities on Panamanian soil, operations must comply with Executive Decree 123 of 1999 (wastewater discharge limits) and Law 41 of 2007 (air emission registration, VOCs, and hazardous waste controls).

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not required for the agent-only offshore leasing model. If a physical office or depot is opened, the following will apply: fire-safety inspection certificate from SINAPROC, municipal construction and occupancy clearance, and occupational health registration with MINSA.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) del Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas; official portal: Sistema Integrado de Tributación (SIT) at https://sit.mef.gob.pa; customs oversight: Autoridad Nacional de Aduanas.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-owned Panamanian S.A. is automatically assigned its RUC (Registro Único de Contribuyente) upon registration with the Registro Público de Panamá under Law 32/1927; activation requires the registered agent to file the initial RUC data in SIT, obtain a digital tax mailbox (Casillero Fiscal), and procure a digital signature (Firma Electrónica) from AIG or an accredited certifier; no physical presence or minimum capital is required; foreign shareholders provide only a notarized power of attorney and passport copies.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No U.S.-style check-the-box or hybrid mismatch election exists under Panamanian law. Available statutory elections: (1) transitional 50/50 tax-credit acceleration on qualifying movable assets (including container boxes) acquired in 2025-2026 under Law 365/2024; (2) voluntary ITBMS registration as 'Responsable' when below the B/.36,000 threshold to enable export zero-rating; (3) election to apply the alternative minimum tax regime under Article 699-A C.F.; (4) exporter-authorization election enabling ITBMS input-credit recovery.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: ITBMS (Impuesto de Transferencia de Bienes Muebles y Servicios)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: B/.36,000 Balboas (pegged 1:1 to USD) of annual gross turnover from taxable activities; compulsory registration for habitual sellers exceeding the threshold and for Gran Contribuyente; voluntary registration allowed for exporters of container-leasing services.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory electronic invoicing via SIT (Facturación Electrónica) for all taxpayers; exporters claiming zero-rating must issue FEV/FES invoices validated through API-based real-time 'convalidación' with SIT, producing an alphanumeric security code and QR code; deferred batch clearance is limited to small taxpayers and must be transmitted within 5 calendar days; lease transactions must be electronically matched to customs export declarations.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods and offshore services qualify for 0% ITBMS. Leased ISO containers departing Panamanian ports on international voyages qualify as exported goods when supported by a customs DUM; container-lease revenue to non-resident shipping lines using the boxes outside Panama qualifies as services used and enjoyed abroad under Article 1056 C.F.; the S.A. must hold authorized exporter status and file the corresponding zero-rated electronic invoice in SIT; input ITBMS on related costs may be recovered through the exporter credit-refund mechanism.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Declaración Única de Mercancías - DUM) filed in the SIA customs system
Bill of Lading or equivalent multimodal transport document evidencing international transit of the container
Inward Remittance Certificate (Certificado de Ingreso de Divisas) or SWIFT/ACH evidence showing lease payment credited to Panama
Zero-rated FEV/FES electronic invoice containing the SIT security code
Exporter registration certificate and SIT Responsible-taxpayer status proof
Packing list and Equipment Interchange Report (EIR) where applicable
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DGI and Aduanas conduct joint audits of zero-rating claims; failure to substantiate exports or to repatriate funds within 180 days triggers clawback of the full ITBMS at the current rate, monthly interest of 10% per annum, fines of 10-30% for late payment, and a 100% surcharge for false documentation; willful evasion incurs criminal penalties of 3-5 years' imprisonment under Article 757-O C.F. plus inclusion in the public Lista de Deudores Morosos.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Panama has no central bank. The Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá (SBP) is the principal banking and financial-system regulator. Exchange control is functionally absent because the U.S. dollar is legal tender and the Panamanian Balboa is a fractional currency pegged 1:1 to the U.S. dollar. International monetary relations are governed under a monetary agreement with the United States.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full currency convertibility with no separate legal tender issuance. Both current-account and capital-account transactions are freely convertible, and there are no exchange control restrictions on inbound investment, ongoing funding, or profit remittance. Container-leasing revenue earned outside Panama is generally treated as territorial-source income and may be repatriated without Panamanian tax, provided proper corporate filings are maintained. Dividends derived from Panamanian-source income are subject to a 10% withholding tax; foreign-source income dividends are non-taxable. No prior central bank approval or exchange allocation requirement applies.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No surrender rules exist. Exporters and service providers, including container leasing companies, may retain proceeds in U.S. dollars or any other currency without mandatory conversion. There is no statutory timeline for repatriation or forced sale of foreign currency. All foreign earnings can be held offshore at the discretion of the company.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Moderate feasibility with legal constraints. Offshore digital Electronic Money Institutions (EMIs) are not directly licensed by the Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá. A Panama-domiciled corporate entity may open accounts with regulated foreign EMIs only if those EMIs comply with correspondent banking relationships and AML/CFT protocols. For cross-border container leasing operations, U.S.- or EU-licensed EMIs (e.g., Payoneer, Mercury, Currencycloud) can be used as collection/disbursement channels, but they are not a substitute for a Panamanian banking account for statutory capital maintenance or legal-merchant registration. The onshore regulatory requirement is that any entity carrying out financial intermediation in Panama must be licensed by the SBP; using an EMI for treasury purposes triggers no Panama licensing but exposes the company to the EMI's jurisdictional KYC/AML requests and potential access restrictions.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Hybrid mandate: a personal KYC interview is mandatory for ultimate beneficial owners or authorized representatives, performed either physically at the bank branch or via a scheduled video conference with notarized identity documents and apostilled corporate records. A full remote account opening without any face-to-face or video interaction is generally not accepted for a first-time corporate account. A local registered agent is required for corporate legalization, and most banks require the physical presence of at least one responsible administrator or grant a power-of-attorney to a Panamanian attorney for the initial appointment. New banking regulations (SBP, 2024) permit remote onboarding with biometric verification, but practice remains conservative; a site visit by the bank officer to the container leasing office is uncommon given the non-residential nature, but can be requested to corroborate operational substance.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inability to demonstrate economic substance. A container leasing company structured as a shell, with no physical offices, no employees, or no audited financials, will be classified as high-risk and may be rejected.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide: (i) physical office lease agreement in Panama or a dedicated registered agent address with explanation; (ii) payroll records or contractor agreements showing employees engaged in leasing operations; (iii) CPA-prepared financial statements reflecting container asset ownership, lease contracts, and cash flow; (iv) list of directors and officers with full disclosure of assets under management.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cryptocurrency-derived capital injection or unexplained source of funds from unreported offshore accounts (flag under SBP anti-money-laundering rules).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit: (i) audited bank statements for the previous 12 months from the funding institution; (ii) signed source-of-wealth declaration with explanation of the capital origin (e.g., sale of container assets, intra-company loans, third-party lease payments); (iii) notarized affidavit from the beneficial owner and supporting contract/sale documents; (iv) tax clearance certificates, if applicable.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions-based cross-border exposure: Leasing counterparties located in jurisdictions subject to OFAC or UN sanctions (e.g., Iran, North Korea, Cuba) may trigger OFAC compliance review at the Panamanian bank.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Produce: (i) full list of container lease counterparties with country of domicile; (ii) compliance policy evidencing no sanctions nexus and screening software or procedures; (iii) export/import licenses for container boxes, if applicable; (iv) signed end-user certificates or trade compliance undertakings from lessees.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant wire transfers for shareholder capital injection must be made via SWIFT MT103 with precise narrative. Recommended purpose code: 'Capital Contribution / Equity Injection' and, for statistical reporting, reference the local investment code 'Inversión Directa' (Panama does not have a formal FX approval requirement). Receiving bank must be a Panamanian licensed bank. The sender's name and account number must match the shareholder of record. For capital from a related company, a loan agreement is required to support a debt injection, while for equity, board minutes from the Panamanian corporation authorizing the issuance of shares must be filed with the bank. Inbound funds are verified via the bank's Know-Your-Depositor process; the bank may request a certificate of seal and incorporation, the corporate ID card, and a sworn statement of first capital contribution.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing rails for trade settlements are primarily through the SWIFT network using MT103 for direct wire transfers and MT700/MT707 for Commercial Letters of Credit (LC). For recurring lease payments, the company may also use Transmittal Letters and direct deposits. Panama's high-value clearing system (ACH) is available for local payments in U.S. dollars, but cross-border payments require correspondent banks (typically U.S. dollar clearings via the Federal Reserve or through a Panamanian intermediary). The company should maintain an operational account with a bank that provides trade finance desks, enabling issuance of standby LCs or performance guarantees for container depot operators. For container box leasing, the predominant form is payment against invoices via SWIFT; commercial LCs are used where the lessee’s credit risk dictates secure settlement.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) in Latin American currencies (e.g., CNY, EUR, MXN, BRL) for container trade exposure
Foreign exchange swaps between USD and EUR, CNY, and GBP
Cross-currency interest rate swaps for long-term lease receivables financing
Exchange-traded currency options (structures available through bank treasury desks)
Deliverable spot transactions (no restriction) for any pair involving USD

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Panama applies a territorial income tax system: resident corporations are taxable on Panamanian-source income only. A container leasing S.A. deriving lease revenue from non-resident lessees for containers used outside Panama will have no taxable income. The alternative minimum calculation (CAIR) applies 8% of attributable deductible costs but does not produce a tax base for pure foreign-source leasing. No statutory tax holiday for container leasing, except the Multinational Headquarters (SEM) regime which may grant a reduced effective rate. Deductible cost allocation is permitted under Article 699 of the Fiscal Code and Executive Decree 170 of 1993.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 101 (Declaración de Renta para Personas Jurídicas) filed electronically via the DGI T-RAX portal or authorized tax software platforms.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due on or before 31 March following the fiscal year-end for calendar-year taxpayers; entities with a different fiscal year must file within three months after fiscal year close.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total gross income from Panamanian-source container leasing activities, including rental income from lessees located in Panama.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter zero if all lease countersigned outside Panama and containers are not physically used within Panama's territory.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Foreign-source income exemption claim (Article 694 of the Fiscal Code).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: State the full amount of exempt foreign-source lease revenue and reference the exclusion; attach a schedule of lease contracts, containers, and revenue allocation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Direct and indirect operating costs attributable to Panamanian-source income, such as local port storage, local maintenance, and local agent fees.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If no Panamanian-source income, report zero and do not deduct costs before computing the CAIR base.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Alternative Minimum Tax Base (CAIR): 8% multiplied by the aggregate deductible costs attributable to Panamanian-source operations.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a zero-revenue, zero-cost foreign-source entity, CAIR equals zero. For partial activity, compute 8% of the local-attribution cost pool.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable income before tax credits: Panamanian-source gross income minus applicable deductions plus the CAIR base.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report zero for pure foreign-source leasing, preserving the documentary evidence of source allocation.
Apply 25% only to Panamanian-source taxable base; no tax on foreign-source profit.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Advance income tax payments (pagos anticipados) already made under Article 117 of the Fiscal Code during the year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident corporations with no Panamanian-source income may have paid USD 0 advance tax; otherwise claim credit for actual installments.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Surcharge for late payment or late filing (recargo), if applicable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident entities filing via a resident agent must ensure that any tax and surcharge is paid in US dollars from a Panama bank account.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing incurs a 10% surcharge on the tax due plus monthly interest equal to the prime rate plus 10 percentage points. Failure to file for two consecutive years is a criminal tax offense. Administrative fines for inaccurate or non-filed transfer pricing forms range from USD 250 to USD 50,000. The statute of limitations for non-filing is 8 years.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% withholding applies to dividends paid out of Panamanian-source profits. A 5% additional surcharge applies to dividends from CAIR-taxed profits. Dividends paid from foreign-source profits are not subject to dividend withholding.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Panama has limited tax treaties. To benefit from a reduced dividend withholding rate, the non-resident shareholder must submit a Certificate of Tax Residence (TRC) from the treaty jurisdiction, complete the DGI treaty relief application, and provide a beneficial ownership statement. The paying entity must forward the documentation before the dividend payment and retain it for five years. Tax authorities may require an opinion or previous certification; if the TRC is not timely filed, the statutory 10% rate applies.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Interest paid to foreign lenders is subject to 10% withholding; royalty payments for IP used in Panama are subject to 12.5% withholding, but a lower treaty rate may apply under a double-tax agreement. For container leasing, lease payments are classified as rental, not royalties, and therefore are not subject to withholding if sourced outside Panama's territory.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Mandatory Local File and transfer pricing affidavit (Form 290) are triggered when the aggregate related-party transactions exceed USD 1 million per fiscal year. A Master File is required for multinational groups with consolidated revenue over USD 15 million. The documentation must be in Spanish, prepared under the arm's-length principle, and filed with the DGI within 6 months after the return due date.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Although Panama has no formal Economic Substance Regulations identical to other Caribbean jurisdictions, its income tax law and the SEM requirements incorporate an economic substance and source-based test. A container leasing S.A. that maintains a physical office, employees, and central management control in Panama while leasing to Panamanian users will be treated as a Panamanian taxpayer. Pure letter-box operations suspect of being a sham are vulnerable to reassessment, fines for incorrect filing, and potential criminal exposure.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Filing a Form 101 that deliberately omits Panamanian-source container lease revenue, fabricating lease documents to misclassify Panamanian-source income as foreign-source, or destroying container movement logs during tax audit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Penalty equal to 50%–200% of the omitted tax under Article 816 of the Fiscal Code, plus interest. Criminal tax fraud under the Criminal Code (Law 14 of 2007) carries imprisonment of 1 to 5 years and a fine. Loss of tax refund offsets and mandatory reassessment with 25% rate.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: A director who signs a false return may be prosecuted as a co-author of tax fraud, subject to fines, civil restitution, travel bans, and imprisonment up to 5 years. Panama permits 'piercing the corporate veil' under Article 52 of the Civil Code where the corporation is a mere instrument of fraud.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating an S.A. with no employees, no physical office, no active banking history, and no legitimate business purpose, particularly when the container fleet is a set of unverifiable foreign assets or the entity interacts only with tax-haven service providers.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: DGI may disregard the corporate entity and assess tax at 100% on attributed non-resident income; fines under the Tax Code for sham invoicing and improper accounting; revocation of the resident agent license; blacklisting as a high-risk entity by the DGI; inclusion in negative public registries.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be ordered by courts to pay unpaid corporate taxes from personal assets; potential criminal sanction for using the company for money laundering or tax evasion; travel restrictions and asset freezing orders can be imposed.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using container lease transactions to disguise illicit funds of third parties, receiving lease payments from shell suppliers, or failing to register the final beneficial owner even when the company is inactive.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fines up to USD 5 million against the entity; criminal seizure of container fleets if linked to laundering proceeds; referral to the UAF and criminal indictment for money laundering under Articles 254 and 255 of the Criminal Code; imprisonment from 5 to 10 years; cancellation of the entity registration.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and beneficial owners who knowingly participate in laundering funds face imprisonment up to 10 years, personal fines, forfeiture of bank accounts, travel bans, and disqualification as corporate officers.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Exceeding the USD 1 million related-party threshold without filing Form 290; submitting materially false transfer pricing documentation; using lease rates that deviate from arm's-length charter rates; failing to disclose ultimate parent entity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fine for failure to file: 10% of the undocumented transaction amount or up to USD 50,000; a 5% to 100% penalty adjustment may be applied to the intercompany charge plus interest of the avoided tax; the DGI may impose an estimated deemed profit and disallow foreign tax credits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Officers who execute documents knowing them to be false may be personally prosecuted for perjury, have a qualified criminal fine, and be barred from serving as officers of Panamanian corporations for 5 years.
